title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability incident follow-up
topics: next steps for logs and benchmark run
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on last night's reliability incident (increased 5xx/timeouts during heavy burst). Discussed root causes (transient upstream backpressure, suboptimal retry policy), immediate mitigation (rate-limit bump, temporary routing to Dedicated pool), and plan for bench runs + longer-term retries and backoff tuning + observability improvements.
next_steps: Redwood to share filtered logs and request ids for the incident by EOD 6/4
Customer to provide traffic pattern and synthetic load script by 6/7
Schedule controlled perf run with Priya and Maya for week of 6/8
Redwood to propose retry/backoff config and rate-limit thresholds by 6/5
action_items: Alex Martinez: Share redwood incident log extract and request IDs (due 2026-06-04)
Priya Shah: Prepare suggested retry/backoff config and docs link (due 2026-06-05)
Maya Chen: Send VPC egress metrics and per-route qps patterns (due 2026-06-07)
Owen Brooks: Provide synthetic load script and peak profile (due 2026-06-07)
transcript: [00:00] Alex Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Alex from Redwood here. We've got Priya and Derek on from our side. How's everybody doing?
[00:06] Liam O'Connor: Hey Alex, doing alright. Bit of a rough morning after that incident last night so appreciate the follow up.
[00:12] Priya Shah: Hi all, quick agenda - recap incident timeline, share logs, go over immediate mitigations and longer term tuning. Then plan a controlled perf run. Sound good?
[00:20] Maya Chen: Yes, that's good. We want to understand root cause - were these 5xxs from Redwood or downstream systems?

[00:28] Alex Martinez: Right. So high level — between 01:15 and 01:45 UTC we saw a spike in 5xx and timeouts for your prod route. Traffic spiked ~4x baseline. Our initial look shows an upstream backpressure scenario; some requests hit timeouts, others returned 5xx from our ingress path. We've collected request ids and sample traces.
[00:42] Derek Liu: There may also have been an interaction with the customer's auth proxy; some of the 502s map to 502 responses from your edge. We're still correlating.
[00:50] Owen Brooks: We did rollout a new edge routing rule yesterday but it was low risk. Could be related though - we'll send the proxy logs.

[00:58] Priya Shah: Important note: the retry policy in the POC defaults is aggressive for short latencies, but during sustained backpressure that can amplify load. We saw retries spike and that contributed to effective qps going up.
[01:10] Maya Chen: That makes sense. Our alerting flagged timeouts first then 5xx after. The pattern looks like cascading retries.

[01:18] Alex Martinez: On the mitigation side we bumped your rate limit for the route temporarily to avoid immediate throttling, and we routed some traffic to your Dedicated pool for more predictable capacity — the 'redwood ded-uh-cated' pool, sorry — my bad on the name, the transcript might say Dedicate, but it's Redwood Dedicated.
[01:34] Liam O'Connor: We noticed latency improved after the bump. But worried about costs if this recurs. We're evaluating whether to go Dedicated permanently or tune hosted settings.

[01:44] Priya Shah: Cost tradeoffs are real. For the POC we can do a mixed approach: short-term Dedicated routing for peak windows + tuning batching and retry/backoff to reduce amplification. Also enable prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts to cut token spend. Note: transcription may say 'kayvee cache' occasionally.
[01:58] Maya Chen: Can you explain what you mean by amplification?

[02:02] Priya Shah: Sure — if a request times out and the client retries quickly, that multiplies the number of in-flight requests, which can overload the runtime and external model endpoints. So we need better client-side backoff and server-side smart throttling.
[02:18] Owen Brooks: On our side we can add jittered exponential backoff. Our frontend currently retries after fixed 200ms for three attempts. Not ideal.

[02:26] Alex Martinez: Great — if you switch to exponential (and add jitter) that should help. We'll share a recommended retry config. Also we want to test lower per-request timeouts to fail fast and reduce queueing.
[02:38] Liam O'Connor: About the 5xx codes — do you have a breakdown of 5xx types? 502 vs 504 vs 500?

[02:44] Priya Shah: Yes — preliminary breakdown: about 55% were 504 timeouts at the ingress, ~30% 502 bad gateway (often map to auth proxy responses), and ~15% internal 500s from the model runtime under memory pressure. We'll send the CSV breakdown.
[02:58] Maya Chen: That internal 500s is concerning - what runtime signals can we inspect? Memory? evictions?

[03:04] Priya Shah: We capture kernel selection logs and memory OOM signals, plus GPU utilization. For this incident GPU utilization spiked but not fully saturated — it looks like queue growth and KV cache pressure were larger factors. We'll annotate the traces to show cache miss rates.
[03:18] Owen Brooks: Can you share example request ids so we can cross-reference with our proxy logs?
[03:22] Alex Martinez: Absolutely — action item for me: share filtered logs and the request ids. We'll redact PII.
[03:28] Liam O'Connor: Thanks. Also curious about rate limits — our app saw a lot of 429s earlier today pre-mitigation. How do you recommend setting thresholds?

[03:36] Priya Shah: We'll propose per-route qps thresholds based on your traffic profile. For bursty patterns we recommend a token-bucket with a higher burst capacity but a lower sustained rate, plus an adaptive limiter that observes drop in success rate. We'll include suggested values in the follow-up doc.
[03:54] Maya Chen: Can Redwood instrument slow requests so we can see client-side vs server-side latency split?

[03:58] Derek Liu: Yes, our tracing shows client->edge, edge->runtime, runtime->model timings. We'll attach trace slices. Note: if tracing IDs are missing we sometimes see Speaker 2 mis-attributed in the transcript.
[04:12] Owen Brooks: For the perf run, what's the recommended test harness? We have a k6 script we use internally.

[04:16] Priya Shah: k6 is fine. If you can provide your script and peak profile we'll run a mirrored perf test from our Hosted and Dedicated pools. We'll also run with KV cache enabled/disabled to measure delta.
[04:26] Liam O'Connor: About timeline — when can we expect the detailed logs and the retry config?
[04:30] Alex Martinez: We'll push logs today and the retry/backoff proposal by Friday 6/5. Priya will own the config doc.
[04:36] Maya Chen: Good. Can we also get a short deck that explains the Dedicated pool cost vs value for this use-case?
[04:42] Derek Liu: We'll provide a concise cost analysis and recommendation for Dedicated vs hosted for your workload. Expect that in the follow-up.
[04:50] Owen Brooks: Any quick wins we can implement immediately?

[04:54] Priya Shah: Immediate wins: (1) adopt exponential jittered retries on client, (2) reduce client-side timeout to fail fast, (3) temporarily increase burst token bucket, (4) enable prefix caching for repetitive prompts. We'll list config snippets.
[05:12] Liam O'Connor: Sounds actionable. One other ask: do you have SLO guidance for 99th percentile latency?
[05:18] Alex Martinez: We recommend 99p SLOs per model/route - e.g., 99p < 600ms for short-context completions; for longer completions it's higher. We'll include measured baselines from the POC.
[05:28] Maya Chen: Are there any security/compliance implications when sharing logs? We need redaction guidance for GDPR-sensitive fields.
[05:34] Derek Liu: We'll redact personal data and share guidance. We support SAML SSO for your console access and log exports can be delivered to your S3 for retention.

[05:44] Alex Martinez: Quick status check — do we have consensus on next steps? I captured: Redwood shares logs+request ids, Priya shares retry/backoff and rate-limit recommendations, customer shares proxy logs and load script, schedule perf run next week. Anything to add?
[05:56] Liam O'Connor: That covers it. Also please include the incident slide with timeline and annotated traces.
[06:02] Priya Shah: Will do. We'll also include a recommended A/B for canarying Dedicated routing — small percent of traffic to Dedicated during peak to test stability.
[06:12] Maya Chen: For postmortem do you want us to include our proxy change notes?
[06:16] Alex Martinez: Yes include it — will help correlation. Also put timestamps in UTC in the postmortem.

[06:22] Owen Brooks: One more note: our frontend retries are not correlated across browser tabs; we may flood the backend if many clients retry simultaneously. We'll add client-side coordination later.
[06:30] Priya Shah: Noted — that's a common pattern. For the perf test we'll simulate many independent clients to reproduce the amplification effect.
[06:38] Liam O'Connor: How will Redwood run the dedicated pool? Is it something we can control?
[06:42] Derek Liu: Dedicated is provisioned by Redwood but you can pin capacity and control autoscale policies; for POC we did a temporary bump. We'll share the config options.
[06:52] Maya Chen: Are there observability additions we should enable? More detailed token-level traces?
[06:56] Priya Shah: Yes, enable token-level cost/latency breakdowns for the route and per-request traces for samples. We'll provide the dashboard link.
[07:04] Owen Brooks: Okay, also let's set a follow-up meeting after the perf run to review results.
[07:08] Alex Martinez: Agreed — propose Wed 6/10 for the results review, I'll send the invite.
[07:12] Liam O'Connor: That works for us. Any blockers?
[07:16] Maya Chen: No blockers other than getting the logs and script.

[07:20] Priya Shah: We'll prioritize logs. One small gotcha in the transcript-generation: sometimes model names show up wrong, e.g., 'Redwood-optimized' might appear as 'red would optimized' — ignore that in the transcript.

[07:30] Derek Liu: Quick note on rate-limit config: we can add adaptive fallback that reduces concurrency to runtime when error rate increases, and route overflow traffic to a lower-cost model variant. That can keep customer traffic online while reducing cost impact.
[07:44] Owen Brooks: Routing overflow to a lower-cost model — is that something we can control per route?
[07:48] Priya Shah: Yes, it's a routing policy you can declare in the route config. We'll share an example.
[07:58] Liam O'Connor: Thanks, appreciate the thoroughness.
[08:00] Alex Martinez: Awesome. We'll follow up with the artifacts. Thanks everyone, we'll adjourn now.
[08:05] Maya Chen: Thanks. Bye.
[42:00] <meeting end>
